katas.title: participantRepository.findById: drop the redundant second check

provenance.find: ## Where site scope is (and is not) enforced

edits.replace:
// list() already scopes by site, and ids are opaque, so a direct lookup is safe.
      return participants.find((candidate) => candidate.id === participantId) ?? null;

defects.scenario: A site-101 coordinator opens /participants/participant-003 (a site-202 subject) by editing the URL.
defects.consequence: findById returns the cross-site participant, and every caller that trusted it (detail page, enroll, complete-study, safety events) now reads or mutates another site's subject. Scoping in list() does not protect lookups by id; ids are guessable sequential mock ids, not secrets.

defects.scenario: In the shipped repository the id lookup re-applies the site scope.
defects.consequence: This line is what makes tests/services/site-scoping.test.ts pass; the patch deletes the only object-level authorization on participant reads (IDOR).

tests.name: site-scoped coordinator cannot read a participant from another site (ported from tests/services/site-scoping.test.ts)
tests.code: const repo = mod.createParticipantRepository([{ id: 'participant-001', siteId: 'site-101' }, { id: 'participant-003', siteId: 'site-202' }]); await assert.rejects(() => mod.getParticipantDetail(repo, mod.demoSessions['user-coordinator-site-101'], 'participant-003'), /Participant not found/);

tests.name: the coordinator still reads their own site and the data manager reads all
tests.code: const repo = mod.createParticipantRepository([{ id: 'participant-001', siteId: 'site-101' }, { id: 'participant-003', siteId: 'site-202' }]); assert.equal((await mod.getParticipantDetail(repo, mod.demoSessions['user-coordinator-site-101'], 'participant-001')).participant.id, 'participant-001'); assert.equal((await mod.getParticipantDetail(repo, mod.demoSessions['user-data-manager'], 'participant-003')).participant.siteId, 'site-202');

katas.title: Blinding: stop masking the treatment arm for roles that enroll

provenance.find: | F10 | Blinding is enforced on read only

defects.scenario: A DATA_MANAGER (the role the shipped UI always calls as), a PI or any coordinator lists participants or opens a detail page.
defects.consequence: Every participant's actual treatment arm is shown to blinded study staff (including subjects they never enrolled, and via listParticipants for the whole site), breaking the blind the TREATMENT_ARM_UNBLIND permission exists to protect. The patch widens a permission by side door instead of fixing the write path F10 complains about.

defects.scenario: The permission matrix grants unblinding only to monitors and pharmacists.
defects.consequence: The service is the single place the matrix is enforced on output (auth-and-permissions.md: 'blinding is enforced in the service output shaping'); OR-ing in PARTICIPANT_ENROLL silently contradicts the matrix without touching it, so a reviewer of permissions.ts would never see the change.
